Communist Propaganda

The following is a summarized translation of the contents of 3 communist handbills which came into the possession of the Municipal Police on November 27, 1933:-

(1) Handbill entitled "A summons to young labourers, peasants, soldiers and revolutionary students in Kiangsu to join the Chinese Communist Youth League," issued by the Kiangsu Provincial Committee of the Chinese Communist Youth League and dated November 7, 1933.
"We are now facing life or death. Foreign aggression and the increased Kuomintang oppression are depriving the people of their means of livelihood. We live only to fight for the success of the Chinese Soviet. The Communist Youth League is the vanguard of the young proletariat. Under the leadership of the Communist Youth League we shall struggle with the Kuomintang, imperialists, landlords, local gentries and capitalists and establish a Soviet Government. Commencing from the October Revolution (November 7) and ending on the Anniversary of Canton Uprising (December 11), the Kiangsu Provincial Committee of the Chinese Communist Youth League is conducting an enrolment movement and is calling upon all to join the League in order to struggle for absolute freedom."

(2) Handbill entitled "Manifesto on the inauguration of the Shanghai Eastern District Young Men's Anti-Imperialist and Anti-Fascist League," issued by the Shanghai Eastern District Young Men's Anti-Imperialist and Anti-Fascist League :-
"As a preventative measure against slavery, we have no other alternative but to unite and put up a determined struggle against imperialism and Fascism whereby China can be saved and our living conditions improved. We, young labourers in the Shanghai Eastern District, organized on November 1 the Shanghai Eastern District Young Men's Anti-Imperialist and Anti-Fascist League and now earnestly request all anti-imperialist and anti-Fascist young masses to join us. Hereunder are some of our principles :-
(a) Oppose dismissal and oppression of juvenile workers.
(b) Demand the release of all anti-imperialist and anti-Japanese warriors.
(c) Demand relief for young men devoid of employment and education.
(d) Organize Young Men's Anti-Imperialist and Anti-Japanese Volunteer Corps.

(3) Handbill entitled "Labour Friends in Shanghai Eastern District," Issue No. 7, dated November 12, 1933, containing articles on victories gained by the Red Army in Szechuen, Kiangsi and Hunan.
